name: Saint Anthony Mary Zaccaria
history: A doctor from Cremona who became a priest and founded the Clerics Regular of Saint Paul, known as the Barnabites after their church in Milan, and an order of sisters. Devoted to Saint Paul and to the Eucharist, he worked to renew the faith of clergy and laity in a troubled age. He died at thirty-six.
life: Anthony Zaccaria was left fatherless as a baby and raised by a devout young mother. He studied medicine at Padua and practised as a doctor in Cremona, caring for the poor, but came to see that souls needed healing too. He taught the catechism, studied theology and was ordained in 1528. Moving to Milan, he joined a confraternity working for reform, and around 1530 founded a congregation of priests dedicated to preaching Saint Paul’s letters and calling people to conversion. It took its popular name from the church of Saint Barnabas, which they served. With Countess Ludovica Torelli he founded the Angelic Sisters of Saint Paul, and he also formed a group of married lay people. He promoted frequent Communion and the Forty Hours’ adoration of the Blessed Sacrament, and the ringing of church bells on Friday afternoons in memory of the Passion. Exhausted, he died in his mother’s arms at Cremona in 1539.
prayerTo: Saint Anthony Mary, physician of bodies and of souls, you loved Christ crucified and burned with the zeal of Saint Paul. Pray for doctors, for priests, and for the renewal of the Church. Help me to read the Scriptures with love and to come often to Christ in the Eucharist. Amen.
penance: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament today, or read one chapter of a letter of Saint Paul slowly and prayerfully.
meditation: He taught that lukewarmness is the great enemy of the soul. In which part of your life have you grown lukewarm?
prayer: Grant us, O Lord God, to learn in the spirit of Paul the Apostle that excelling knowledge of Jesus Christ, by which St. Anthony Mary, himself wondrously learned, gathered together in Your Church new families of clerics and virgins. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
